clusters.title: Doc and comment drift against the tree (documentation-§5), addon and library sites
clusters.recommendation: One sync-docs pass per repo; replace restated counts and line numbers with symbol or source pointers instead of refreshing them.
clusters.cluster_summary: Every finding but the regenerated RESULTS.md line reproduces. All of them come from one habit: prose and comments restate derivable figures (file counts, line counts, minors, kit revisions, shim counts) and file:line citations, and these rot on the next edit. That is why WG-A-03 reopened and AT/BL/KC/PM recur. The fix lands per repo, as one sync-docs pass in each, and should replace restated counts and line numbers with symbol names or pointers to the owning source (LibKa0s.xml, run.lua, the provenance line, test-cases.md Totals) rather than refresh them. Behavioral falsehoods (AM launcher left-click, PM lifecycle comments, MM Slash.lua:857, WG Compat load order, BL saved-view model, PC LibStub sentence) are the must-read parts. The shim-count rule is already explicit at documentation.md:279-292 (mechanical grep over the addon's own Compat.lua; LibKa0s shims not counted or re-documented), so PFE (14) and WG (9) need no upstream decision. An optional upstream SHOULD in WowAddonStandards documentation-§5, 'cite by symbol, do not restate derivable counts', would cut recurrence but does not replace the local passes.

clusters.cluster_summary: v2.61.0 widened line-endings-§3 to require both *.sh and *.py text eol=lf. The standard's own .gitattributes and five whole-body restatements were never updated, and neither was dev-copilot's audit agent check (c). The root-cause fix is a single WowAddonStandards commit: replace .gitattributes with the line-endings-§5 non-client body byte-for-byte (WAS-R-01 + WAS-A-04), and fix the five enumerations, preferably by citing line-endings-§3 instead of restating it (WAS-R-02 absorbs WAS-A-05/06/07). The same commit can harden check (e) quoting and scope the §7 EOL-gate MUST. dev-copilot then needs one follow-up edit to its agent spec, covering check (c) and the check (e) quoting copy. Nothing breaks at runtime: no collection repo tracks a .py file, so everything here is low severity.

clusters.title: Test-kit --list Totals count declared skips, contradicting the badge
clusters.recommendation: Fix renderTotals in LibKa0s (kit 37->38); addons clear it on re-vendor with regenerated test-cases.md.
clusters.cluster_summary: Root cause: LibKa0s testkit/framework.lua renderTotals (line 569, Kit.VERSION 37, HEAD 353f286) prints #tests, the whole registry, including declared skips. Its renderInventory preamble (:576-577) calls that number the authoritative pass count the badge must match, which contradicts testing-§5 and the kit's own docblock at :204. So every consumer with a declared skip ships an inventory Total one above its correct badge (verified: KickCD 1303 vs 1302, PanelMaster 1036 vs 1035, and others). The single fix lives in LibKa0s: Total counts non-skipped cases, a Skipped row is added when any exist, the header is reworded, a kit self-test is added, Kit.VERSION goes 37->38 and it ships in this remediation's LibKa0s minor release. Each addon then clears its finding with the whole-tree tests/_kit re-vendor it gets anyway, regenerating docs/test-cases.md in the same commit. No local edits. Severity is low: only a generated doc row is wrong, and badges and gates are correct.

clusters.title: Standard internal contradictions and section-coverage claims
clusters.recommendation: One WAS documentation-and-playbook consistency pass; WAS-A-08, WAS-A-14, WAS-R-05 are the should items.
clusters.cluster_summary: Sections of the standard, its playbooks and its summaries were edited one at a time, and duplicated lists (frozen stores, Tier 2 members, applicability enumerations, ordinals, the pre-adoption launcher census) have drifted apart. Every fix lands in WowAddonStandards: one documentation-and-playbook pass covering AUDIT.md, launcher.md, slash-commands.md, documentation.md §3/§6/§8, library-stack.md §7, NEW_ADDON_CONTEXT.md and the two summaries. Must or should: the stale launcher 'expect findings' wording (WAS-A-08), the §6 frozen-store list and sweep (WAS-A-14) and the scaffold runner comment (WAS-R-05). The rest are cheap consistency fixes to fold into the same pass. LibKa0s and dev-copilot need no change.

clusters.title: Addon doc-set structure (documentation-§1/§2/§3) and release notes
clusters.recommendation: One small docs commit per addon (LH, PM, PFE, MM); delete the contributor-facing release lines.
clusters.cluster_summary: All eight findings are real, local doc-shape or release-note drift. Each fix belongs in the addon's own README.md, CLAUDE.md or docs/, and no single upstream change would make any of them moot. Two of them are recurrences that an upstream check would prevent: SD-FIN-01's sync-docs pass deleted PFE's empty Tier 3 table, and PM has reintroduced angle-bracket placeholders. Those checks are optional dev-copilot follow-ups, not blockers. Recommendation: one small docs commit per addon (LH: README close, 1.4.0 row and map list; PM: placeholders, 1.2.0 row and stub order; PFE: Tier 3 heading; MM: release-note sentence), each followed by a de-AI pass. Delete the contributor-facing 'Released on lint, tests and complexity only' lines in LH and PM rather than prefixing them. Correct MM's sentence to the old path actually shipped, minimap.hide, and to its real value semantics. The PFE settings-panel reshape is optional.

clusters.title: Hub ARCHITECTURE.md past the ~400-line spill guideline
clusters.recommendation: Spill AM and LH Module Map sections; trim MM and PFE; the rest are guideline overshoots.
clusters.cluster_summary: Re-measured on the feature branches: all seven hubs are 422-578 lines. Only two mandated sections break the documentation-§3 ~60-line spill MUST: AuraMaster Module Map (94 lines, mostly drag/snap/detach data-flow narrative) and LootHistory Module map (78 lines, duplicating module-map.md). Both are cheap per-repo spills. The rest are SHOULD-level overshoots, which documentation.md:344 says to report by shape and not by arithmetic ('1071 lines, not 412'). Their only real defects are duplication and stale history: PFE's 1609-char re-vendor narrative, PM's census band dispositions copied from RESULTS.md, and retired-row narratives left in the MM/PM/PC registers. Recommendation: fix AM and LH, and trim MM and PFE together with their sibling items. Optionally add one sentence upstream in WowAddonStandards documentation-§3 saying that retiring a register row means deleting it and leaving its history in the cited bundle, and have the dev-copilot audit playbook stop filing hubs under ~450 lines when no section breaches the spill. That stops the MM/PM/PC regrowth.

clusters.title: Rotted cross-repo citations and worked examples in the standard and specs
clusters.recommendation: Add a WAS citation-form SHOULD and convert broken citations to it; companion dev-copilot example fix; no full recount.
clusters.cluster_summary: Root cause: the standard has no citation-form rule, so present-tense file:line citations and counts rot with every release, and dev-copilot's worked examples copy the same habit. The single best fix is one WowAddonStandards pass. It adds a documentation SHOULD (present-tense claims cite a symbol or heading; historical claims pin Repo@sha:path:line), converts the broken citations to that form instead of renumbering them, past-tenses or deletes the claims that are now false (LSMPatch, Schema.lua:1553), and folds in WAS-A-10, WAS-R-09, AT-A-14 and LK-A-08. dev-copilot gets a companion commit, scoped to the worked examples that steer generated output. Do not do a full recount.

clusters.title: Standard changelog, index and citation hygiene
clusters.recommendation: Fix live citation errors in one WAS commit; changelog move (WAS-R-03) is gated on owner approval and dev-copilot H-01.
clusters.cluster_summary: Every finding is real and every fix lands in WowAddonStandards. The only ordering dependency is that dev-copilot H-01 must land before the changelog move. The one finding with recurring cost is WAS-R-03: 92% of the index (384 KB) is changelog, and every audit, review and harvest run reads it. Moving it to its own file is worth doing, but the review bundle still marks C-02 'owner decision required', so it goes to the owner as a should, gated on approval and on H-01. The live-text citation errors (library-stack.md:223 and AUDIT.md:994 citing documentation-§5 for the scheme in §6, and documentation.md:259 citing item 8 for item 6) should be fixed in one citation commit. WAS-A-13 and WAS-R-12 overlap, so merge them. The changelog typos, the reorder and the README wording go into the C-02 move when it lands, or into a small standalone edit if it does not. Replace the footer date with no date at all. The TL;DR rename is not worth doing on its own.

clusters.title: Issue-store housekeeping: stale labels and contradicted declines
clusters.recommendation: One throttled label-fix pass on six closed issues; comment on KC#11 and PC#8.
clusters.cluster_summary: Six closed issues across AuraMaster (#22), PanelMaster (#47) and LibKa0s (#32, #33, #37, #39) still carry an open-only status label (state:untriaged or state:triaged). The cause is that issues get closed with a bare gh issue close or a commit keyword, and neither swaps the label. dev-copilot's issue-summary already reports a closed issue with an open-state label as an Inconsistency and deliberately leaves the fix to a person, so no upstream code change is needed. The fix is one throttled pass of label edits recorded in exceptions.tsv. A one-line rule in dev-copilot saying 'closing an issue also swaps its state label' is optional. Two closed declines that the code has since overtaken (KickCD#11, PrettyChat#8) are worth a comment each in the same GitHub pass, with their labels left alone. AT-A-12 is refuted because #26 already carries the 2026-09-24 scope comment. AT-A-17 is a healthy backlog, not a finding.

clusters.title: Slash command argument parsing and output shape
clusters.recommendation: Fix AM-R-05 (delete resolves name before id); MM-R-05 doc line; rest optional polish.
clusters.cluster_summary: Seven independent per-repo slash nits with no shared root cause and no upstream fix that would make them moot (LibKa0s-Slash only formats rows; each addon parses its own arguments). Only AM-R-05 needs a code fix: a destructive delete can hit the wrong container when a container has a bare-number name. The fix is to copy MultiMeters' WindowManager.Resolve order (name first, then id) and refuse when the two disagree. MM-R-05 is a documented design limit with a working id-based workaround, so it needs a doc line only. KC-R-03 is sanctioned by the standard (slash-commands.md:87, debug-logging.md:344). It and the rest are optional polish to fold in only when the files are already being touched.

clusters.title: Library-absent stubs and unreachable fallbacks
clusters.recommendation: Fix cheap stub MUST breaches (AM-A-07, PM-A-03, LH-A-04, AT-A-07 Option A); U-3 stays an optional design question.
clusters.cluster_summary: The stub regime comes from library-stack.md (one setup file per adopted module, degrading to a stub) and testing-§8 (a parity case per adopted module). Packaging never strips LibKa0s, but under library-stack.md the major also goes absent when a module misses its floor or raises at load, for example on client API drift. So the stubs are reachable in rare runtime failures, not only on a hand-damaged install, and an open-evolutions question (U-3) will not retire them soon. U-3 is filed as an optional upstream design question and does not block anything. The cheap per-repo MUST breaches (AM-A-07, PM-A-03, LH-A-04, AT-A-07 Option A) are fixed now against the current standard rather than deferred. AT-A-16 is dead defensive code and is left alone.

clusters.title: Release gate: functions above CCN 15
clusters.recommendation: Extract helpers in AM and BL; phase LH by file with characterization tests first; PC at 15 is fine.
clusters.cluster_summary: Each repo crossed the automated-tests-§3 tag gate (zero sighted functions above CCN 15, blindFiles 0) through its own recent commits, so the fix is per-repo and no upstream change applies. AuraMaster has 1 function over (18), BankLedger has 1 (16, reported twice as BL-A-02 and BL-R-01, now merged into one item), and LootHistory has 26-27 introduced since f31727b (2026-10-01), several by the v13 migration. These are real regressions, not old debt that sighting exposed: convertHolderMoves, accumulateLedger and planHolder did not exist at f31727b. PrettyChat's listSettings sits at exactly 15, which does not breach the gate. Recommendation: fix AM and BL with named-helper extractions. Phase LH by file, writing a characterization test first and taking the v13 migration last. Track any guard-ladder function that can only get under 15 through metric-driven splitting (#52) as a deviation, so the tag gate stays meaningful.

clusters.title: Files approaching the 1500-line cap
clusters.recommendation: One pure-move peel per hot file (AM, BL, LH) and refresh stale watch-list rows in the same commit.
clusters.cluster_summary: No file breaches the cap. Under layout-§1 (layout.md:57,71), a file in the 1000-1500 band is compliant and on notice, and the band is dispositioned in the automated-tests watch list. The real trigger for acting is each repo's own watch-list disposition, which has fired or gone stale: AuraMaster RESULTS.md:112 says 1327 against an actual 1406, BankLedger RESULTS.md:103 says 1221 against 1427, and LootHistory RESULTS.md:103-104 records re-check triggers at 1400 and 1300 that have both been passed. The fix belongs in each repo and has no upstream route. Do one verbatim pure-move peel per hot file (AM Database migrations, BL Browser per-tab views, LH BrowserTable grouping layer) and refresh the stale watch-list rows and ARCHITECTURE census sentences in the same commit. Fold BL-A-06 into BL-R-02. The AM drag test split and the LH Browser.lua widget-kit peel are optional.

clusters.title: Bare or malformed standard citations (documentation-§6)
clusters.recommendation: Fix MM (architecture-4) comment (must); rest optional or refuted.
clusters.cluster_summary: These are leftovers from earlier citation sweeps, so each fix belongs in the repo that has it. No upstream fix makes them unnecessary, and a per-addon guard test is the wrong tool because it would reject the continuation form the standard uses itself ('debug-logging-§8/§9'). One item must be fixed: MultiMeters has a malformed '(architecture-4)', which breaks the MUST grade, and correcting it is a one-character comment edit. The other work is optional polish. KickCD has standalone bare §N sites in its tests and live docs. LibKa0s has a payload file:line citation, which should ride the next Slash.lua change (#43) and not justify a release of its own. The ConsumableMaster finding is refuted because its sites are continuations of the same kind the standard writes. The PartyFrameEnhanced finding is an observation and needs no work.

clusters.title: Perf stand-down lifecycle edge cases
clusters.recommendation: Fix LH Coalesce flag and PM combat-held unlock across stand-down; LibKa0s and AT items optional.
clusters.cluster_summary: These are separate per-repo lifecycle gaps, and no single upstream root fixes them. In each case, state armed before or during a stand-down (a Coalesce pending flag in LootHistory, a combat-held unlock in PanelMaster, a debug-hold timer in AbsorbTracker) outlives NS.StandDown. LH-R-04 and PM-R-06 are real bugs that players can see, cheap to fix locally, and should be addressed. The LibKa0s template's suspended=false is NOT dead: the current Perf host contract (rule 2, surface table) still endorses reading perf.suspended, and PartyFrameEnhanced and KickCD read it. So the upstream change is reduced to an optional comment refresh, and AT's vacuous assertion should be retargeted at NS.IsStoodDown(), not deleted along with the stub field.

clusters.title: Secret-value handling and test support
clusters.recommendation: Fix WG Compat cooldown reader to decide on isActive and return unknown when secret (must); LibKa0s testkit simulator first.
clusters.cluster_summary: Root cause: WhatGroup's Compat.GetSpellCooldownRemaining does a comparison and arithmetic on GetSpellCooldown's startTime and duration, which can be secret in combat, and it never checks the plain isActive 5th return that LibKa0s Compat's contract tells callers to decide with. The real fix is local to WhatGroup (WG-R-01). It should not return 0 ('ready') when the values are secret. It should decide on isActive and return an 'unknown' signal so the ticker stays armed. Support work: LibKa0s adds an additive testkit secret simulator (WG-R-09) first, and WhatGroup's regression tests then use that simulator after re-vendoring (WG-R-02). The standard's §8 named list gets a hygiene addition (WG-R-08). The finding's claim that audits downgrade this class is wrong, because §8 already has a catch-all and the defect is a comparison, not pre-formatting. MultiMeters' diagnostics-only isLocalPlayer compare (MM-R-07) is optional and should be folded into its F-006 PlainTruth export.

clusters.title: Hot-path allocation and over-broad event registration
clusters.recommendation: Only CM OnSpecChanged unit filter is worth doing; others optional or refuted.
clusters.cluster_summary: These are separate per-repo micro-costs with no shared root cause, so no upstream fix applies and each fix belongs in its own repo. Only CM-R-07 is worth doing: ConsumableMaster's OnSpecChanged ignores the unit argument, so a groupmate's respec triggers a full recompute and a SPEC_CHANGED broadcast. KickCD already filters this case, and copying its guard costs two lines. AT-R-02 and KC-R-09 are cheap, safe tidy-ups that can be done optionally. PFE-R-06 is mostly wrong because strings are interned and ApplyDriver already checks for equality. MM-R-09 is refuted as a defect: the behaviour is documented on purpose and the standard permits it.

clusters.title: Raw lizard quoted as the complexity check
clusters.recommendation: Quote the runner, not raw lizard, in five addons; un-pin lizard in MM.
clusters.cluster_summary: Five addons still quote the raw lizard command in reader-facing docs: suite tables in docs/automated-tests/README.md, docs/testing.md, DEPENDENCIES.md setup blocks and, in MultiMeters, docs/performance.md. automated-tests-§3 (MUST) and anti-pattern #92 require every quoted gate line to be the runner, 'bash tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh --suite complexity'. The standard already states this rule, so no upstream change is needed and each fix is a per-repo docs edit. Frozen superpowers plans that quote raw lizard are historical and stay untouched. Fix all five as cheap 'should' items. MultiMeters also pins lizard==1.24.0, which breaks the documentation-§7 MUST, and the standard's own text rebuts the pin's stated rationale, so un-pin it. An optional follow-up outside this cluster: Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks/CLAUDE.md:87 quotes the same raw line, and a dev-copilot sync-docs/revendor-standards check could flag raw 'lizard -l lua' in non-frozen docs.

clusters.title: Destructive/reset actions: scope and confirmation
clusters.recommendation: Fix PM delete-all popup text now (must); reset sweep and per-panel Delete confirmation test-first.
clusters.cluster_summary: Every finding is a local UX or reset-path gap in one addon, and no LibKa0s seam would make any of them moot, so each fix lands in its own repo. PanelMaster carries the real work. Its delete-all popup says 'on this character', but the AceDB profile is the shared 'Default', so the text understates the reach to every character on a default install. Its global reset skips the session-only rows that options-ui-§12 requires it to sweep, and the tests are too thin to catch that. Its per-panel Delete and Reset have no confirmation, and a Registry comment wrongly says Reset is confirmed. Recommendation: fix PM-R-02 now; do PM-A-01 and PM-A-02 together, test first; fix the PM-R-05 comment and add a confirmation for per-panel Delete. PrettyChat's Categories Defaults is already documented and is the owner's call.

clusters.title: Debug-logging change gates and load-time logging
clusters.recommendation: Add one DebugAtEnable migration summary line in AM; rest compliant or optional.
clusters.cluster_summary: There is no shared root cause. Each finding is a per-repo debug-logging detail, and no LibKa0s change makes any of them moot. Only AuraMaster's migration lines are a real diagnostic gap. Its [Migrate] lines run only from OnInitialize, while State.debug is false, so they never reach the log, which leaves the debug-logging-§8 Lifecycle coverage (schema migration) unmet. Fix it with one DebugAtEnable summary line. AbsorbTracker's two hand-rolled memos are an optional SHOULD-level cleanup. The ConsumableMaster and PartyFrameEnhanced items are compliant as written, and nothing needs to be done for them.

clusters.title: Deviation register rows and unresolvable evidence ids
clusters.recommendation: Fix unresolved register citations in AT, CM, LK; PFE after owner confirms D9.
clusters.cluster_summary: All four findings are documentation-only register hygiene in per-repo deviation registers: citations that do not resolve or point at unrelated findings (CM, LibKa0s), a stale per-profile-stamp row (AbsorbTracker) and wording nits (PFE). The recurring cause is cross-repo consolidation ids (WS-02, LibKa0s-A-*, cross-repo LK-29/LK-30) written back into per-repo registers, where they collide with or fail to resolve against the repo's own audit ids. The fixes land per repo as small edits to the citation cells. An optional upstream guard (audit-review-history: qualify a cross-repo plan id with its bundle path or cite the commit sha) would stop the problem recurring, but it does not make the per-repo fixes unnecessary. Do AT, CM and LK in this pass and fold PFE in alongside them once the owner confirms D9.

clusters.title: Byte-wise string handling breaks non-Latin locales
clusters.recommendation: Fix PM ASCII-only slug with a UTF-8-aware duplicate guard; KC UTF-8 truncation helper; rest optional.
clusters.cluster_summary: The root cause is the same in each repo: Lua string functions (%w, #, sub, lower, date %b) work on bytes or the C locale, not on UTF-8 characters, so each addon fails in its own place. No single upstream fix covers all four. The one item that matters is PanelMaster's ASCII-only slug: every fully non-Latin panel name gets the same frame name, so only one such panel can exist. Fix it in PanelMaster together with a UTF-8-aware duplicate guard. KickCD's byte-count truncation should get a file-local UTF-8 prefix helper modelled on MultiMeters' utf8Truncate, not a new LibKa0s surface. AuraMaster's post-translation :lower() and the LibKa0s chart's %b default are latent, so they are optional at most (a comment, and one line in the API doc).

clusters.title: Dead compat fallback rungs on removed AddOns globals
clusters.recommendation: Delete dead AddOns-global fallback rungs in LibKa0s (Env, OptionsIdList), MM and PM.
clusters.cluster_summary: The bare AddOns globals (GetAddOnMetadata, IsAddOnLoaded, GetNumAddOns, GetAddOnInfo) were removed from the client in 11.0, and every admitted client is Interface 120100. Every fallback rung that calls one of them sits behind a C_AddOns rung that answers first, so it is unreachable dead code under compat.md's v2.65.0 MUST. compat.md:9 is correct and names this exact GetAddOnMetadata rung as its worked case. The defect is LibKa0s/Env.lua:52-53, which claims the global is 'still present'. Nothing goes upstream to WowAddonStandards. The fix lands in three places. In LibKa0s, delete the Env and OptionsIdList rungs, bump to Env minor 2 and IDLIST minor 4, rewrite the comment, fix the tests and docs, and ship in this run's LibKa0s release; every addon then picks it up on re-vendor. MultiMeters and PanelMaster each delete their own host-side rungs. An owner /dump of the four globals on live retail is a cheap confirmation to fold into the smoke pass, but it does not gate the work, because the standard has already ruled on it.

clusters.title: Event-frame discipline (events-frames-taint-§1)
clusters.recommendation: Move PFE watcher to AceEvent target; wrap WG bare RegisterEvent; PC refuted.
clusters.cluster_summary: Two of the three findings are real §1 breaches, and both are small. PFE keeps a private CreateFrame watcher even though it embeds AceEvent, which §1 line 36 forbids explicitly. WG has one bare self:RegisterEvent left outside the pcalled helper. Each fix is local to its repo. No upstream change is needed, because §1 already answers PFE's (event, target) collision: use a separate AceEvent target, as PFE's own Providers.lua does. PC-R-12 is refuted. PrettyChat embeds no AceEvent, so its named watcher falls under the carve-out, and no rule forbids naming a frame.

clusters.title: Pre-formatted chat lines (events-frames-taint-§8)
clusters.recommendation: Optional; fix sites only when the file is already being edited, via NS.Format.
clusters.cluster_summary: Printer calls in three addons build the chat line with .. or :format before calling the shared printer. Every value formatted is addon-owned or typed by the player, so none of the sites is in the §8 combat-protected trigger set. That makes them SHOULD NOT observations with no behaviour change and no way to expose a secret value. I read every site. AbsorbTracker's and LootHistory's are as cited. Of BankLedger's six, three are not real deviations: Slash.lua:253 and :339 carry comments citing §8 that explain why they are written that way, and DebugLogSetup.lua:51 is a localized whole-sentence format. None of these needs to be addressed. Fix the remaining sites in each repo only when the file is already being edited in this run, using the secret-safe NS.Format (the library's printer.Format) for :format sites so the wording does not change. Separate printer arguments are joined with spaces, so splitting would print 'v 3'. Optionally, WowAddonStandards AUDIT.md could also stop reopening sites outside the trigger set as per-repo findings.

clusters.title: NaN/inf and unvalidated numeric input
clusters.recommendation: Three local finiteness and grammar guards (LibKa0s parseNumber, PM, CM).
clusters.cluster_summary: All three findings come from the same pattern: a bare tonumber() at a trust boundary. Lua 5.1 tonumber accepts 'nan', 'inf', '1e999', hex and exponent forms, and nothing downstream rejects them. The cluster names LibKa0s as the root-cause home, but only LK-R-06 actually goes through the LibKa0s SlashParse seam. PanelMaster's COERCE.number, Clamp and freeNumber are its own code, and ConsumableMaster's problem is ID grammar rather than finiteness. So the right plan is three small local fixes, not one upstream fix: LibKa0s parseNumber rejects non-finite values (C-04), PanelMaster adds finiteness guards and a non-finite branch in recover, and ConsumableMaster whitelists ^%d+$ / ^[sS]:%d+$. All three should be addressed. None is a must, because each needs deliberate unusual input, and WoW's tonumber('nan') behaviour is still unverified (smoke NUM-3).

clusters.title: Named non-setting state and schema version targets
clusters.recommendation: Fix LH schema.md writer sentence; KC rename optional; PM refuted.
clusters.cluster_summary: Three per-repo naming gaps with no shared root cause and no upstream fix. LootHistory's schema.md says holdings has one writer ('Reconciler:Flush only'), which is false: ForgetHolder (the Forget popup) and MarkLoginGenesis (LoginScan) also write it, so that sentence should be fixed. KickCD's migration target is named CURRENT_DB_VERSION instead of the standard's NS.SCHEMA_VERSION. The value is correct, so this is an optional consistency rename, best done if KickCD is already being edited. PanelMaster is refuted: the Settings Schema section spills to docs/schema.md as documentation-§3 sanctions, and schema.md already gives minimapPos its key, owner (core/LauncherSetup.lua) and writer and act (LibDBIcon, on drag).

clusters.title: versioning-git trunk-based MUST vs feature-branch practice
clusters.recommendation: Revise versioning-git trunk-based rule in WAS with full ripple; makes DC-A-12 moot.
clusters.cluster_summary: versioning-git.md:13 requires trunk-based work and allows branching only 'when the human explicitly asks'. WowAddonStandards/CLAUDE.md:116-117 uses a looser judgment trigger ('when a changeset genuinely warrants isolation'). dev-copilot/CLAUDE.md:111, Ka0sAddonsCommonTasks/CLAUDE.md and /dev-copilot:finalize all make same-named feat/<date>-<topic> branches, merged --no-ff and then deleted, the standing flow. The cause is a single stale rule in WowAddonStandards, so the fix is one revision there, carried through the full ripple. That revision makes the per-repo finding DC-A-12 moot, so no per-repo deviation rows are needed.

clusters.title: British spellings in live docs (localization-§5)
clusters.recommendation: British-spelling sweep in LibKa0s (extend prose gate, fix register); dev-copilot sweep optional.
clusters.cluster_summary: Live authored prose in LibKa0s (two adoption docs) and dev-copilot (commands, agents, profiles, root docs and one script comment) uses British spellings, which breaks the localization-§5 MUST. Each repo has its own cause: LibKa0s's own prose gate (tests/test_prose.lua) does not list the two adoption docs, and its register row 3 wrongly treats adoption-prompt.md as a frozen record; dev-copilot has no prose gate at all. Each fix stays in its own repo: a mechanical sweep with the canonical testkit/prose_lists.lua lists, plus, in LibKa0s, extending the gate and correcting the register. No upstream change makes either item moot. Address LibKa0s as should; dev-copilot is worth a cheap sweep (optional+), prioritizing step headings that seed generated bundles.

clusters.title: Combat-time preview/profile edge cases
clusters.recommendation: Guard PFE PROFILE receiver against combat unlock; AT RelockForCombat optional.
clusters.cluster_summary: In both addons the combat re-lock lives only in the PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED / OnEnterCombat handler, so any path that puts an unlocked state in front of the frames after combat has started leaves preview on for the rest of the fight. The fixes are per-repo and small. PFE-R-01 is real but reached by a different route than the review cites: '/pfe profile use' (LibKa0s Slash.lua:776) and the Profiles page (Options combat cover) are already gated, but '/pfe profile copy <unlocked profile>' (settings/Slash.lua PROFILE_VERBS.copy) has no combat check. It copies locked=false, fires OnProfileCopied, then adoptProfile publishes PROFILE and Preview.lua:198-204 calls applyLock(true) mid-fight. Recommendation: guard in the PFE PROFILE receiver, which covers every path, and include the AbsorbTracker RelockForCombat extraction in the same batch as an optional consistency fix.

clusters.title: AbsorbTracker — perf test fidelity and UX

AuraMaster is the only collection addon that leaves its screenshots out of its ignore list: the other 11 already ignore them, either as media/screenshots or, in Outfitter, as Media. So no upstream route is needed, and the reality lens was wrong to say the gap is collection-wide. The options-ui-§17 deviation is ratified and still valid, and needs no action. Recommendation: make one small AuraMaster commit that fixes both .pkgmeta lines, then re-run packaging checks (a) to (c).

The per-class seed test that let CM-R-02 through is fixed in the same commit (CM-R-08). Running discovery on spec change (CM-R-04) is a cheap should-fix. The flyout score cache (CM-R-03) is downgraded to low: the mock's nil tooltip makes every call a pending refetch, and in the client TooltipCache memoizes resolved tooltips. The composite-config dedup (CM-R-05) is optional cleanup, since its divergence cannot be reached.

clusters.cluster_summary: Every finding is confirmed and every fix belongs in MultiMeters. The one real defect is MM-R-01: with Merge pets on, the owner's own-source setCell overwrites a cell that foldPet created earlier, so a pet that ranks above its owner loses its numbers. Fix it together with its red-first test MM-R-02 in a single commit. MM-A-08 does not route upstream: the conformance step 8 RightButton drive is a per-addon test, the menu mock is addon-local, and the other 10 addons already drive RightButton in tests/test_disabled.lua. MultiMeters is the only one that does not, so the fix is local. MM-R-03, MM-R-04 and MM-R-08 are cheap fixes worth doing. MM-R-06 is optional tidying.

clusters.title: PanelMaster — sanitizer and enabled-state correctness
clusters.recommendation: Add four REPAIR rules and a template-coverage property test in PM.
clusters.cluster_summary: PanelMaster's REPAIR table in modules/Registry.lua drives both R.Sanitize and R.SanitizeField, but it has no rules for four template fields: accentColor, accentBorderColor, artBlend and artDesaturate. As a result, a missing key or a junk value in these fields survives sanitizing and R:CopyFrom copies it to other panels. The renderer already guards all four, so what the user can see is limited to the editor swatch, the panel dump and copied junk. The fix lives in PanelMaster alone. It is about four lines of rules plus a property test that every C.PANEL_TEMPLATE key either has a repair rule or is explicitly exempt. Separately, the enabled==nil display mismatch in the two list sites is cosmetic and optional.

clusters.title: PartyFrameEnhanced — secure-write queue robustness and profile rebuild
clusters.recommendation: Isolate PFE flushSecure per entry with xpcall; drop redundant ResetProfileCounted.
clusters.cluster_summary: The root cause is in PartyFrameEnhanced's flushSecure (core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:92-106). It runs queued closures with no per-entry isolation and clears pending[key] lazily, so one raise orphans every later key for the rest of the session and skips the post-flush PublishVisibility. The defect is real but latent: no trigger is known. Fixing it per-entry with xpcall(fn, geterrorhandler()) also neutralises the queue-level impact of PFE-R-03. PFE-R-05 is a separate cheap cleanup, the redundant ResetProfileCounted after SetProfile in /pfe profile new. All three fixes belong in PartyFrameEnhanced and can share one work item. No upstream route applies.

clusters.title: PrettyChat — cross-addon globals, settings validation, savedvars and comments
clusters.recommendation: Rebuild LootHistory chat-pattern caches when source globals change (must); small PrettyChat fixes.
clusters.cluster_summary: Every finding in this cluster is real. The only serious one is PC-R-01. LootHistory compiles the loot, currency and roll-won patterns from the chat globals once and never rebuilds them, but PrettyChat rewrites those globals in the middle of a session, so LootHistory stops recording loot until the next /reload. The fix belongs in LootHistory/core/Util.lua as a cache keyed on the source strings, and PrettyChat needs no code change. The PrettyChat items are small local fixes: refuse a blank format (PC-R-02), skip pruning when the stored stamp is newer than this build (PC-R-04), correct the false taint sentence (PC-R-05) and correct the wrong figures in comments (PC-R-06). PC-R-13 does not need fixing.

clusters.title: WhatGroup: test buttons clobber state, tooltip and comment drift

clusters.cluster_summary: RunTest (core/WhatGroup.lua) writes the sample into pendingInfo. That overwrites a real capture, and while the addon is stood down it leaves a withheld popup that the StandUp re-show arm displays unasked. Both problems are fixed in WhatGroup in one commit: RunTest renders the sample through the existing previewInfo/shownInfo path as a one-shot, never touches pendingInfo, and only prints the chat preview while stood down. The lifecycle test is rewritten to assert behaviour. The tooltip and comment drift (WG-R-05, WG-R-07) are cheap edits that ride along in the same file pass. No upstream route.

The pane-resize double render (LK-R-04) is structurally confirmed but cheap and resize-only. Its optional fix is host-side in LootHistory, and it needs no library seam.

clusters.title: LibKa0s — Autocomplete hooks, callbacks and options

The doc fix is required. A generation-guarded re-hook is optional hardening, and the testkit mock already drops hooks on SetScript. findings.title: /am delete 3 deletes container #3 even when a different container is named "3"
findings.evidence: findContainer treats any numeric arg as an id (tonumber(arg) -> FindContainer(id)) while the name validator accepts '3'; a bare-number name can never be matched by name, and delete is destructive with no AceDB undo. Reachable only with a bare-number container name addressed by name on the CLI.
findings.remediation: C-04: '#N' always means id; resolve exact name match first; if a numeric arg matches one container's name and a different container's id, refuse with a new enUS ambiguity line naming both; document precedence in docs/slash-dispatch.md rows 12 and 14; 4 new cases in tests/test_slash_verbs.lua (badge 2049 -> 2053, regenerate docs/test-cases.md). Rejected: forbidding numeric names.
findings.cluster_title: Slash command argument parsing and output shape
findings.assessment: Verified: findContainer (settings/Slash.lua:169-170) returns FindContainer(tonumber(arg)) before any name match, while the validator accepts a name like '3'. So '/am delete 3' can delete a different container than the one named '3', and AceDB has no undo. The case is rare, but the result cannot be reversed, and MultiMeters' Resolve already does name-first.
findings.verdict_remediation: In findContainer, try an exact (case-insensitive) name match first and fall back to the numeric id. If a numeric argument names one container and is the id of a different one, refuse with one new enUS line naming both. Make '#N' always mean an id. Update the precedence note in docs/slash-dispatch.md rows 12 and 14. Add 2-4 cases to tests/test_slash_verbs.lua, and update the badge and docs/test-cases.md in the same commit. Do not forbid numeric names.

findings.assessment: The behaviour is real but it is a documented design decision (settings/Slash.lua comment above WINDOW_VERBS.copy; docs/slash-dispatch.md:75), not a bug. findings.verdict_remediation: Documentation only: in docs/slash-dispatch.md:75 (and optionally the WINDOW_USAGE text), say that the source may be given as its window id, which covers default names with spaces. Make no parser change.

findings.cluster_title: Slash command argument parsing and output shape
findings.assessment: The mechanics are verified (core/KickCD.lua: refuse(...) then runDebug(self, "") toggles the console). The only nit is that KickCD does both, printing a refusal and also toggling, and the test hides that with a re-toggle.
findings.verdict_remediation: Optional: choose one sanctioned behaviour. Either refuse and print the sub-verb list without toggling (split the list printer out of the bare branch), or toggle silently. Then pin it in tests/test_slash.lua in place of the 'toggle it back' workaround.

findings.title: Teleport-cooldown reader compares cooldown values that can be secret in combat, killing the popup ticker and aborting the join notice
findings.locations: core/Compat.lua:109-112; modules/Frame.lua:587-589 (ticker); core/WhatGroup.lua:828 (chat Teleport row), :1026/:1041 (ShowNotification before ShowFrame)
findings.evidence: Compat.GetSpellCooldownRemaining does 'if start <= 0 or duration <= GCD_SECONDS' and arithmetic with no IsSecret guard; LibKa0s Compat.lua:232-233 documents startTime/duration/modRate as possibly secret in combat. Harness probe with comparison-raising values: './core/Compat.lua:112: attempt to compare table with number' from both the ticker and ShowNotification. AceTimer reschedules only after callback returns, so the ticker dies; the details link row, auto-show popup and combat defer never happen. modules/Diagnostics.lua:21 already acknowledges the hazard. findings.remediation: Add Compat.IsSecret guard arm (library's IsSecret, else three-line issecretvalue stub per anti-patterns #47); GetSpellCooldownRemaining returns 0,false when either value is secret; ticker skips unreadable ticks keeping its text and staying armed; Teleport row omits the tag when unreadable. findings.cluster_title: Secret-value handling and test support
findings.assessment: Verified at WhatGroup/core/Compat.lua:110-114: `start <= 0 or duration <= GCD_SECONDS` and `(start + duration) - GetTime()` run on values that LibKa0s Compat.lua:232-233 says may be secret, with no IsSecret guard. A raise kills the AceTimer ticker and aborts ShowNotification before ShowFrame. Severity is medium because no one has confirmed in the client that a teleport cooldown is secret, and the bug needs a join that happens in combat (smoke S-001). The proposed '0,false when secret' would report a teleport that is on cooldown as READY, so it is corrected.
findings.verdict_remediation: In Compat.GetSpellCooldownRemaining, also take the 5th return isActive. When start or duration is secret (Compat.IsSecret: the library's IsSecret, or the 3-line issecretvalue stub when the library is absent), do no arithmetic. Return an 'unknown' signal (for example nil plus isActive) and do not return 0. Have the chat Teleport row and the popup button decide 'on cooldown' from isActive. findings.title: Util.Throttle allocates an args table on every call, including every SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN
findings.evidence: pendingArgs = { n = select('#', ...), ... } is built even with no arguments, which is always the case for Cooldowns; one small table per cooldown event in combat. Unmeasured: tests/perf.lua has no OnCooldownEvent scenario and committed captures predate current code.
findings.remediation: Measure first: add an OnCooldownEvent perf scenario; only if it shows a per-event allocation worth removing, reuse a shared empty-args sentinel when select('#', ...) == 0.
findings.cluster_title: Hot-path allocation and over-broad event registration
findings.assessment: Confirmed: core/Util.lua:190 allocates `{n=select('#',...), ...}` on every wrapped() call, including calls that coalesce. Cooldowns calls it with no arguments for SPELL_UPDATE_COOLDOWN, SPELL_UPDATE_USABLE and SPELL_UPDATE_CHARGES. That is one tiny table per event in combat, which the incremental GC collects with no visible cost. A zero-arg sentinel is safe because fire() only reads args.n and unpack, and it does not break the guarantee that each burst keeps its own args.
findings.verdict_remediation: Optional: hoist `local EMPTY_ARGS = { n = 0 }` (never mutated) and set `pendingArgs = select('#', ...) == 0 and EMPTY_ARGS or { n = select('#', ...), ... }`. A perf scenario is not required for a two-line change that cannot alter behaviour. Add a unit test that a zero-arg throttle still fires fn once per burst.

findings.title: Cast-bar name truncation counts bytes, not characters
findings.evidence: 'if #name <= maxChars ... string.sub(name, 1, maxChars) .. "…"' under a label 'Truncate after (characters)'. Accented names cut early on deDE/frFR/esES/ptBR; ruRU at ~half, koKR/zhCN/zhTW at ~a third; cut mid-sequence yields invalid UTF-8. Opt-in (default 0); secret names skip truncation. MultiMeters already has a private utf8Truncate.
findings.remediation: Decision needed: Option A, an additive LibKa0s-Core Utf8Prefix helper (preferred if this cycle ships a LibKa0s release; MultiMeters can adopt it too), with a library-absent arm in the degraded stub; or Option B, a file-local utf8Prefix counting lead bytes. Update the stale comment at :332-333. Tests: TruncateName('Éclair de givre', 3) == 'Écl…', valid UTF-8, plus a CJK case; badge and inventory move in the same commit.
findings.cluster_title: Byte-wise string handling breaks non-Latin locales
findings.assessment: Confirmed. truncateName uses #name and string.sub under a 'Truncate after (characters)' label, and its comment admits it can cut mid-character. The feature is opt-in (default 0) and secret names skip it, but once it is turned on, ruRU and CJK clients get broken glyphs and a cut at roughly 2 to 3 times fewer characters than the label promises. MultiMeters already has a proven pure-Lua utf8Truncate. Two call sites do not justify a new LibKa0s surface with a degraded-stub arm.
findings.verdict_remediation: Option B: add a file-local UTF-8 prefix helper to KickCD/modules/Castbar.lua that counts lead bytes (mirroring MultiMeters/modules/Row_NameCell.lua utf8Truncate) and rewrite the stale comment at :332-334. Add tests: TruncateName('Éclair de givre', 3) == 'Écl…', valid UTF-8 output, and a CJK case. Promote it to a LibKa0s helper only if this cycle is already cutting a LibKa0s release for other reasons.

findings.title: Non-Latin panel names collapse to one frame name; only one can exist
findings.evidence: %w is ASCII-only, so Cyrillic/Hangul/Han names slug to '' -> 'Panel' -> PanelMaster_Panel_Panel; second such panel (and an English 'Panel') refused. Accented pairs (Ärger/Örger) collide. Measured in scratch probe3.lua. No test covers non-ASCII.
findings.remediation: Address: make slug preserve/encode non-ASCII bytes (unique per name) for newly created panels; existing frame names stamped on records unchanged; add tests; smoke LOC-2/LOC-6.
findings.cluster_title: Byte-wise string handling breaks non-Latin locales
findings.assessment: Confirmed in code. Util.Slugify uses gsub('[^%w]+','_'), so Cyrillic, Hangul and Han names all fall back to 'Panel', and frameNameTaken refuses the second one. Accented pairs such as Ärger/Örger collide too. The player sees a clear refusal message, loses no data and can work around it by renaming into ASCII, so medium fits better than high. The smoke rows are LOC-1 to LOC-5; LOC-6 does not exist.
findings.verdict_remediation: In Util.Slugify, encode the non-%w bytes (for example per-byte hex) so every distinct name gets a distinct slug. Apply it only to newly created or stamped frame names and leave existing records unchanged. In the same change, keep a duplicate-name guard that does not depend on the slug: today the Slugify comment relies on FindByName's ASCII-only lower() plus the slug collision to reject case variants. Without it, 'Übersicht' and 'übersicht' become two panels, against LOC-3. Add headless tests for Cyrillic and CJK uniqueness and for the Ärger/Örger pair. Owner smoke: LOC-1, LOC-2, LOC-3 and LOC-5. Reference PanelMaster#26.

findings.cluster_title: Event-frame discipline (events-frames-taint-§1)

findings.title: Stand-down's owed-Hide PLAYER_REGEN_ENABLED registration is a bare self:RegisterEvent, outside the pcalled NS.SafeRegisterEvent helper

findings.title: Panel number fields accept NaN/±inf; /pm recover cannot repair NaN
findings.evidence: tonumber('1e999')=inf, NaN passes Clamp and freeNumber; stored, passed to SetSize/SetPoint, written to SV. recover reports 'moved 1 panel' forever for NaN x. Measured in probe.lua. SV serialization of non-finite unverified (smoke NUM-3).
findings.remediation: Address: reject non-finite numbers in COERCE.number / Clamp / freeNumber at the trust boundary; add tests.
findings.cluster_title: NaN/inf and unvalidated numeric input
findings.assessment: Verified: COERCE.number (settings/PanelSchema.lua:40-44) is a bare tonumber, and Util.Clamp (core/Util.lua:16-22) returns NaN unchanged because both comparisons are false. NaN then persists through freeNumber, R:SetPosition (Registry.lua:817) and Canvas, and /pm recover reports 'moved' on every run because NaN ~= NaN. Clamp does bound +/-inf on clamped fields, so the stuck-recover case needs NaN specifically, but corruption that keeps reporting itself and cannot be repaired justifies medium severity.
findings.verdict_remediation: Add a local isFinite(n) (n == n and n ~= math.huge and n ~= -math.huge) and use it in COERCE.number (reject with 'expected a number'), Util.Clamp (non-finite falls back to fallback, then lo), freeNumber and R:SetPosition. Make RecoveredOffsets/IsOffScreen/Recover treat a non-finite x/y/w/h as needing a reset, so one recover run repairs it and the next run reports nothing. Add tests for nan, inf, -inf and 1e999. Keep smoke NUM-3 (SV serialization of non-finite values) open for the owner. Does not depend on LK-R-06.

findings.title: ParseValue accepts nan/inf and the write seam stores them on an unbounded number row; clamp absorbs NaN only by argument order
findings.evidence: Lua 5.1: tonumber('nan'/'inf'/'1e400') -> nan/inf/inf. math.max(-100,0/0) -> -100 but math.max(0/0,-100) -> -nan, so order is load-bearing and unrecorded. Row with no min/max/validate stores the non-finite value; SV serialization unverified. Only via '/<slash> set <path> nan' on an unbounded row; none confirmed; WoW tonumber('nan') unverified.
findings.remediation: C-04: parseNumber rejects nan and +-inf with existing ERR_NUMBER before enum/clamp logic; add a comment recording why math.max(row.min, n) argument order matters; add tests in tests/test_slash_parse.lua. Not in Schema.Set (type-agnostic by design).
findings.cluster_title: NaN/inf and unvalidated numeric input
findings.assessment: Verified in LibKa0s/LibKa0s/SlashParse.lua: line 128 is a bare tonumber(args[1]). The clamp at :140-141 absorbs NaN only because n is the second argument to math.max/min, and nothing records that. An unbounded number row stores nan/inf through the shared write seam. Only an explicit '/<slash> set <path> nan' on such a row can trigger it, but the seam is shared by every addon, so a single cheap fix covers the whole collection.
findings.verdict_remediation: C-04: in parseNumber, reject n ~= n, n == math.huge and n == -math.huge with the existing ERR_NUMBER before the enum and clamp logic. Add a comment recording why the math.max(row.min, n) argument order matters. Add tests/test_slash_parse.lua cases for nan, inf, -inf and 1e400. Leave Schema.Set type-agnostic. Ship in the next minor bump and re-vendor through the normal flow; per-addon re-vendoring is not urgent for this fix alone.

findings.title: /cm priority accepts any tonumber token: zero, negative, fractional, hex, exponent
findings.evidence: 0, 1.5, 0x10, 1e3 and raw -20484 are written into added/blocked; raw negative becomes a spell sentinel without s: prefix; fractional ID builds /use item:1 via %d; panel's IdInput validates so the two doors disagree.
findings.remediation: C-06: accept only ^%d+$ (positive) or ^[sS]:%d+$; reject others with the existing usage line; new slash test.
findings.cluster_title: NaN/inf and unvalidated numeric input
findings.assessment: Verified: parsePriorityID begins at core/SlashCommands.lua:197 and falls through to a bare tonumber(token) at :205 (so the cited line is the defect line). The add, remove and move paths (:378, :399, :416) all use it, so 0, 1.5, 0x10, 1e3 and raw negatives (which become spell sentinels without the s: prefix) end up in the persisted added/blocked lists. A NaN token would additionally raise 'table index is NaN'. The slash door also disagrees with the panel's IdInput validation. This is an ID-grammar fix that LibKa0s cannot make moot.
findings.verdict_remediation: C-06: accept only ^%d+$ with a value greater than 0, or ^[sS]:%d+$ with a value greater than 0; return nil for anything else so the existing usage line prints. Preferably share one validator with the panel's IdInput. Add a slash test covering 0, 1.5, 0x10, 1e3, -20484, nan and a valid s:123.

findings.cluster_title: Combat-time preview/profile edge cases
findings.assessment: Confirmed: the only re-lock is in addon:OnEnterCombat (core/AbsorbTracker.lua:318-321), and neither StandUp nor OnEnable in core/Lifecycle.lua touches `locked`. A mid-combat stand-up, or a /reload on an unlocked profile, therefore shows the placeholder and suppresses repaints (Display.lua:437) until the next combat. Reaching it is narrow (the profile must have been unlocked out of combat with no fight since), it fixes itself at the next pull, and no standard rule requires the fix. Worth batching with PFE-R-01 for consistency, but not required.
findings.verdict_remediation: Extract the re-lock body from OnEnterCombat into NS.RelockForCombat(), which returns whether it re-locked. Call it from OnEnterCombat, keeping the either/or that publishes VISIBILITY/REPAINT only when it did not re-lock. Also call it at the end of StandUp and OnEnable when UnitAffectingCombat('player') is true. Add 2 test cases with red-under notes.

findings.title: A profile switch during combat turns preview on mid-fight, bypassing the combat refusal
findings.locations: modules/Preview.lua:198-204 (PROFILE handler); modules/Preview.lua:126 (NS.AcceptLock), :95; settings/Slash.lua:307; core/PartyFrameEnhanced.lua:302-311; modules/CastBars.lua:263
findings.evidence: PROFILE handler calls applyLock directly, skipping AcceptLock's InCombatLockdown refusal; PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED re-lock has already fired. Cast bars show 'Preview cast' placeholders for the rest of the fight. Reachable via /pfe profile use or Profiles page in combat to a profile stored unlocked. No test covers it.
findings.remediation: C-001: in the PROFILE receiver, when locked==false and InCombatLockdown(), NS.SetByPath('locked', true) and print the combat re-lock line; else applyLock as today. Two new cases in tests/test_profile_switch.lua (455->457).
findings.cluster_title: Combat-time preview/profile edge cases
findings.assessment: The PROFILE receiver (modules/Preview.lua:198-204) does skip NS.AcceptLock's combat refusal, but both cited triggers are already gated. '/pfe profile use' goes through LibKa0s ProfileSwitch, which refuses in combat (Slash.lua:776-778), and the Profiles page is behind the Options combat cover. One route is still open: '/pfe profile copy <name>' has no combat check, so copying an unlocked profile mid-fight runs CopyProfile, then OnProfileCopied, then adoptProfile, then PROFILE, then applyLock(true), and preview turns on for the rest of the fight. A third-party SetProfile can also reach the receiver. The trigger is rare, so the severity is low, but the fix is one cheap branch that makes the combat guard hold on every path.
findings.verdict_remediation: In the PROFILE receiver (modules/Preview.lua), when enabled and stored locked==false and InCombatLockdown(), write NS.SetByPath('locked', true) and print the existing combat re-lock line. Otherwise call applyLock as today. Add 2 cases to tests/test_profile_switch.lua that drive the receiver through OnProfileCopied (the '/pfe profile copy' path) in combat: one with an unlocked source, one with a locked source. Each case gets a red-under note.

findings.title: Offline 'coalesced repaint' and 'zero-overhead' perf scenarios measure a test-written fan-out, not shipped doRepaint
findings.evidence: All three scenarios call NS.UpdateAbsorbBar via a test closure; repaintPass bracket never measured. 48.0 B/iter matches a 1-upvalue closure (scratch probe 48.8 B); doRepaint's shape probes at 144 B, above the 72 B ceiling. performance-§9 requires the hottest bracketed path.
findings.remediation: C-1: suite seam NS.Timer.__doRepaint; add repaintPass scenario, move probeOverheadOff/On onto it, rename old paintPass to paintBars, re-derive PROBE_OFF_BYTES_CEILING, update docs/performance.md:72-77.
findings.cluster_title: AbsorbTracker — perf test fidelity and UX
findings.assessment: Verified. paintPass (perf.lua:196-197) and probeOverheadOff/On (perf.lua:224-229) each wrap NS.UpdateAbsorbBar in a test closure, and doRepaint has no seam (grep finds only NS.Timer.__ev). The zero-overhead gate therefore never runs the outer repaintPass bracket, the parent derivation or doRepaint's closure, and a regression there cannot turn it red. Shipped behavior is unaffected and the paintBar bracket is still exercised, so this is a test-fidelity gap and should be graded low, not medium.
findings.verdict_remediation: Add a test-only seam, NS.Timer.__doRepaint = doRepaint, following the NS.Timer.__ev pattern. Add a repaintPass scenario and point probeOverheadOff/On at the seam, re-arming pending as needed. Re-derive PROBE_OFF_BYTES_CEILING from a fresh measurement using the documented measured/ceiling/margin triple, keeping the margin under the 64 B cost of one table. Do not reuse the reviewer's 144 B scratch figure. Update the scenario table in docs/performance.md (~lines 72-77). Keep the bar-level scenario, with its 12-API-call assertion. Renaming paintPass to paintBars is optional and only worth it to avoid confusion with the repaintPass label.

findings.title: Changing Master scale may move dragged bars (unverified in-client)
findings.evidence: Saved offsets are in the bar's own scaled space and restored unchanged, so SetScale should scale the distance from anchor. Follows from client semantics; smoke S-05 settles it; regrade to Medium if confirmed.
findings.remediation: C-6 only if S-05 confirms: store positions in screen units with a savedvariables-§1 ladder step v6, docs/schema.md, tests. Close with no change if refuted.
findings.cluster_title: AbsorbTracker — perf test fidelity and UX
findings.assessment: The code matches the claim. savePosition (Bar.lua:21) stores raw GetPoint offsets, RestoreBarPosition (Display.lua:153-169) reapplies them unchanged, and UpdateBarAppearance calls bar:SetScale(NS.GetMasterScale()) (Display.lua:234), so a scale change should shift a dragged bar's distance from its anchor. It is still unverified in-client, it shows up only when the Master scale setting changes, it is common WoW frame behavior and it loses no data. Any work therefore waits on the owner's smoke check S-05.
findings.verdict_remediation: Wait for the owner to run S-05. If refuted, close with no change. If confirmed, start with the cheaper fix: in the Master scale setter, rescale each stored offset by oldScale/newScale, or re-anchor so the bar keeps its on-screen position. That needs no schema change. Use the savedvariables-§1 ladder step v6 (screen-unit positions, plus docs/schema.md and tests) only if offsets must also survive other scale sources, such as UI scale.

findings.title: 26 MB of media/screenshots ships in the package (observation, owner's call)
findings.evidence: Seven PNG/JPG files totalling 26 MB (E-9) ship in every download; the client cannot load PNG/JPG and the README links screenshots from media.forgecdn.net. No rule fails: layout-§4 names media/screenshots/ as legitimate and packaging's template does not mention it.
findings.remediation: Owner's decision: if accepted, add '  - media/screenshots' to .pkgmeta; if the collection agrees, propose the same line for packaging's minimum template upstream.
findings.cluster_title: AuraMaster: packaging and recorded deviation
findings.assessment: The 26M of unloadable PNG and JPG files does ship in every download, and the README uses forgecdn copies. The reality lens said the gap is collection-wide. That is refuted: AbsorbTracker, BankLedger, ConsumableMaster, KickCD, LootHistory, MultiMeters, PanelMaster, PartyFrameEnhanced, PrettyChat and WhatGroup all ignore media/screenshots, and Outfitter ignores Media. findings.title: Every ApplyView / tab switch recomputes the window two or three times
findings.evidence: ApplyView leaves the 0.2 s search debounce armed (SetSearchText cancels it); SelectTab repaints what SwapTabState painted. Cost unmeasured; mock SetText does not fire OnTextChanged (tests/wow_mock.lua:261). Reviewer: Optional, cheap.
findings.remediation: C-03: shared dropFilterDebounce() used by SetSearchText and ApplyView; SelectTab refreshes only when prev == name; +2 cases.
findings.cluster_title: BankLedger: browser perf, search and backfill
findings.assessment: Confirmed. ApplyView calls SetText (:879), which in the client arms the 0.2 s debounce through OnTextChanged, then calls ApplyFilterNow (:882) without cancelling the timer, so the same filter runs a second time. SelectTab (:238-242) repaints LedgerTable and Insights after SwapTabState has already refreshed them. This is redundant work with no correctness impact, and the cost has not been measured.
findings.verdict_remediation: C-03, in the same Browser.lua commit as C-04: a shared dropFilterDebounce() helper used by both SetSearchText and ApplyView. In SelectTab, skip the redundant LedgerTable:Refresh/Insights:Refresh only on a real switch (prev ~= name) and still call RefreshFilterOptions on History. Add two test cases and no perf instrumentation. Skip C-03 if Browser.lua is not being edited.

findings.title: Search filter matches untrimmed text while suggestions trim
findings.evidence: Typing 'linen ' empties the table while list offers Linen Cloth. Reviewer: Optional.
findings.remediation: C-04: searchClause(t) helper used by OnTextChanged, SetSearchText, buildActiveFilter; +1 case.
findings.cluster_title: BankLedger: browser perf, search and backfill
findings.assessment: Confirmed in code. OnTextChanged (Browser.lua:1096), SetSearchText (:666) and buildActiveFilter store the raw text, Database textOK (:457-461) does a plain lowered substring find, and _rankSuggestions trims first (:607-608). The cited example is wrong, because 'linen ' is a substring of 'linen cloth'. Leading, trailing-after-last-word or doubled whitespace (' linen', 'cloth ') does empty the table while the suggestions still offer Linen Cloth.
findings.verdict_remediation: C-04: add a searchClause(t) helper that trims (and returns nil when the result is empty), and use it in OnTextChanged, SetSearchText and buildActiveFilter so the query and the suggestions normalize the same way. Add one test case using ' linen' or 'cloth '.

findings.title: Login backfill always spends its 40-id budget on oldest ids; unresolvable ids could starve it
findings.evidence: Needs 40 distinct unresolvable ids; 30-day retention self-heals on default profile. Reviewer: No, record only.
findings.remediation: None; record only.
findings.cluster_title: BankLedger: browser perf, search and backfill
findings.assessment: Confirmed. Backfill.Collect walks oldest-first and caps at BACKFILL_MAX_IDS = 40, and unresolvable ids are never marked, so they are retried first on every login. Starvation needs 40 or more distinct unresolvable ids. Retention, which is account-wide in db.global (retentionDays = 30, not a profile setting), ages them out, except when retention is set to Always. The case is theoretical and has never been observed.

findings.title: Per-profile macro fingerprint skips writes to account-wide macros holding another profile's body or deleted entirely
findings.evidence: alreadyApplied compares only KCM.db.profile.macroState, never the live macro. Two scratch repros fail today ('expected #showtooltip\n/use item:950001, got ... item:950002'; deleted KCM macro not recreated). Docs promise each character rewrites on arrival. Affects any multi-character per-character-profile user on login, and any player deleting a KCM_* macro; macro bar and actual macro disagree.
findings.remediation: C-01: add liveBody(macroName) via GetMacroIndexByName/GetMacroInfo (unprotected reads) and only trust the fingerprint when the live body equals it; three new tests; doc paragraph in docs/macro-manager.md; confirm in-client the client does not normalize stored bodies.
findings.cluster_title: ConsumableMaster — correctness, data seeds and recompute cost
findings.assessment: Verified at MacroManager.lua:442-445 and :516: alreadyApplied compares only the per-profile macroState, and returns 'unchanged' before any live read. A deleted macro, or one that another profile overwrote, is therefore never rewritten, which contradicts scope.md and README.
findings.verdict_remediation: Add liveBody(macroName) using GetMacroIndexByName/GetMacroInfo, and trust the fingerprint only when the live body matches. On a mismatch or a missing macro, fall through to the existing combat-aware write path. Add three tests and a paragraph in docs/macro-manager.md. Add an owner smoke check that the client does not normalize stored bodies.

findings.title: Devourer Demon Hunter spec (12_1480) has no stat-priority seed; ranks as Agility with no secondaries
findings.evidence: Only 12_577 and 12_581 seeded; fallback [12]='AGI', secondary={}. Devourer (spec 1480) is the Intellect spec; FLASK, STAT_FOOD, CMBT_POT and WPN_ENCH ranking prefer Agility and lose all secondary preference for any Devourer without an override.
findings.remediation: C-02: add ["12_1480"] = { primary = "INT", secondary = <archon.gg order per file header refresh procedure> }; secondary order must be sourced, not guessed.
findings.cluster_title: ConsumableMaster — correctness, data seeds and recompute cost
findings.assessment: Defaults_StatPriority.lua seeds only 12_577 and 12_581. Devourer (1480, an Intellect spec) falls back to CLASS_PRIMARY_FALLBACK[12]='AGI' with no secondaries, so every Devourer without an override gets the wrong consumable ranking.
findings.verdict_remediation: Add ["12_1480"] = { primary = "INT", secondary = <order sourced via the file header's archon.gg refresh procedure> }. If no sourced order is available, ship INT with an empty secondary list, note the gap, and do not guess.

findings.title: Every out-of-combat recompute re-ranks every category for flyouts with no score cache (63% of pass allocation)
findings.evidence: Collector-stopped attribution: Pipeline.Recompute 226715.5 B/iter (184 tooltip fetches); MacroBar.Refresh alone 142727.7 B, 20 ListAvailable and 107 C_TooltipInfo.GetItemByID calls per refresh; flyout off 105509.3 B, bar off 83910.5 B. Flyout rebuild ~121 KB of 226.7 KB. Out-of-combat only; no frame-time capture.
findings.remediation: C-03: MB.Refresh builds one scoreCache={fields={}} (out of combat only) and passes it via FO.Apply -> FO.Candidates -> Selector.ListAvailable; new test asserting one tooltip parse per candidate per refresh; optional barRefresh perf scenario.
findings.cluster_title: ConsumableMaster — correctness, data seeds and recompute cost
findings.assessment: Structurally true: each flyout re-scores through ListAvailable with no scoreCache. The magnitude is a mock artifact, though. wow_mock.lua:1003 returns nil from GetItemByID, so TooltipCache.Get stores a pending stub and refetches on every call. In the client, resolved tooltips are memoized (TooltipCache.lua:436-485). What remains is out-of-combat re-scoring and GetItemInfo churn, with no frame-time evidence.
findings.verdict_remediation: Defer unless a perf-analysis capture shows recompute frame time that matters. If done: build one scoreCache per out-of-combat MB.Refresh, thread it through FO.Apply -> FO.Candidates -> Selector.ListAvailable, and test one scoring pass per candidate per refresh (not one tooltip parse). Any perf figure needs a mock that returns real tooltip lines.

findings.title: Spec change runs no discovery pass, so unseeded bag consumables are missed for the new spec until bags change
findings.evidence: OnSpecChanged only requests a recompute; discovery is filed per spec and runs on PEW, BAG_UPDATE_DELAYED, GET_ITEM_INFO_RECEIVED, stand-up and /cm resync. Scratch repro fails: 'expected 961701, got nil' after spec switch. Self-heals on next bag change.
findings.remediation: C-04: call runAutoDiscovery("spec_changed") before requestRecompute in KCM:OnSpecChanged; new pipeline test; update docs/data-flow.md event row.
findings.cluster_title: ConsumableMaster — correctness, data seeds and recompute cost
findings.assessment: Verified that KCM:OnSpecChanged (ConsumableMaster.lua:767-776) only calls requestRecompute. Discovery is filed per spec, so the new spec's bucket misses unseeded bag items until the next bag event. It heals itself, but the fix is a single call.
findings.verdict_remediation: Call runAutoDiscovery("spec_changed") before requestRecompute in KCM:OnSpecChanged. Add a pipeline test and update the event row in docs/data-flow.md.

findings.title: Composite config resolution written twice; flyout copy compositeRefs is the max-CCN function (15)

findings.cluster_title: ConsumableMaster — correctness, data seeds and recompute cost
findings.assessment: There are two copies of the composite config rule. Their divergence on a missing bucket cannot be reached under AceDB defaults, and compositeRefs is at CCN 15 (at the threshold, not over it), so players see no effect.

findings.title: Cast bar keeps a stale primary-icon anchor after the icon grid empties
findings.evidence: 'if payload.primaryIcon ~= nil then inst.lastGridLayout.primaryIcon = payload.primaryIcon end' treats nil (real 'no primary icon' from an empty grid, IconGrid.lua:495) as 'field absent', so the cache keeps a pooled button that was ClearAllPoints()ed and Hide()n; resolveGridFrame fallback never reached. On default anchorMode PRIMARY, the cast bar likely disappears until an icon returns or /reload (unverified in client). Reached by disabling/removing every spell or swapping to a spec with no learned spell. No test covers Castbar:OnGridLayout.
findings.remediation: Copy primaryIcon unconditionally (including nil) into lastGridLayout; add a characterization test over Castbar:OnGridLayout that an empty grid falls back to resolveGridFrame. Owner smoke check in client.
findings.cluster_title: KickCD — cast bar, glow gate, defaults and lint
findings.assessment: Verified: Castbar_Events.lua:254 copies primaryIcon only when non-nil, while IconGrid.lua:495 announces nil for an empty grid. The cache therefore keeps a released, unanchored pooled button, and ApplyAnchor never reaches the resolveGridFrame fallback on the default PRIMARY mode. No test covers OnGridLayout.
findings.verdict_remediation: In Castbar:OnGridLayout, assign inst.lastGridLayout.primaryIcon = payload.primaryIcon unconditionally (including nil), and update the misleading 'defensive' comment. Add a characterization test: drive OnGridLayout with a populated payload, then with primaryIcon=nil, and assert that ApplyAnchor anchors to resolveGridFrame. Record an owner in-client smoke check (empty the spell list or switch to a spec with no learned spell, cast bar stays visible) and do not mark it passed.

findings.title: Glow gate ignores casts by a non-attackable target while the target_casting trigger counts them
findings.evidence: Gate keyed on IsHostileUnitCasting (false when UnitCanAttack is false) and resolveInterruptible returns early when neither moved; target_casting trigger uses inst.isCasting() (any cast). For a friendly/non-attackable caster the tuple stays (false, nil), so RefreshAllGlows never calls UpdateGlow; glow off at start, stale at end. Default trigger is 'never'.
findings.remediation: Optional: owner decides whether target_casting means any cast or a hostile cast. If hostile, fix the trigger; if any, include the raw casting state in the gate tuple.
findings.cluster_title: KickCD — cast bar, glow gate, defaults and lint
findings.assessment: Real mismatch: the gate tuple uses IsHostileUnitCasting, while the target_casting trigger uses any cast. The default trigger is 'never', the effect is a cosmetic missing or stale glow, and the right fix depends on what the owner intends target_casting to mean.
findings.verdict_remediation: Owner decision. If target_casting means a hostile cast (likely for an interrupt tracker), make the trigger use State.IsHostileUnitCasting so it matches the gate. If it means any cast, add the raw casting state to the RefreshAllGlows gate tuple. Add a characterization test for the chosen semantics.

findings.title: CONFIG_CHANGED{general} rebuilds Cooldowns on scale/alpha slider ticks and grid drags

No general row changes what Cooldowns polls; 'enabled' already reaches it through the stand-down latch and Resume rebuilds. Every throttled tick pays a full re-poll and SPELL_STATE fan-out. findings.remediation: Optional, low value: narrow the condition to section == 'spells', with a characterization case proving 'enabled' still rebuilds via Resume.
findings.cluster_title: KickCD — cast bar, glow gate, defaults and lint

But it is config-time only, throttled and unmeasured, and narrowing it risks the 'enabled' rebuild path. That is not worth it without a perf-analysis capture showing hitches.

findings.title: New default spell lists never reach existing profiles

A spec added to defaults/Spells.lua later would give existing profiles an empty grid silently. Nobody affected today: every shipped spec has been in the defaults since 1.0.0.
findings.remediation: Defer. Re-check trigger: the first spec added to defaults/Spells.lua after 1.4.0; then seed missing (class, spec) pairs individually.
findings.cluster_title: KickCD — cast bar, glow gate, defaults and lint
findings.assessment: Real latent design gap, but no profile is affected: no spec has been added to defaults/Spells.lua since launch. The finding itself recommends deferring until a trigger fires.
findings.verdict_remediation: No code change. File a KickCD GitHub issue (state:triaged, severity:low) recording the trigger: when a spec is first added to defaults/Spells.lua, seed missing (class, spec) pairs individually in Database:BuildSpells.

findings.title: .luacheckrc whitelists 22 read-globals no shipped file reads
findings.evidence: 22 read_globals names have zero readers among the 50 shipped files; GameFontDisable and UIDropDownMenu_AddButton (legacy dropdown API) have zero readers anywhere, tests included; the rest are read only under tests/. A new bare call to those globals would lint clean. Continues prior review F-016.
findings.remediation: Drop the two dead names and move the test-only names under files["tests/"]; luacheck stays 0/0.
findings.cluster_title: KickCD — cast bar, glow gate, defaults and lint
findings.assessment: The lint slack is real, but the review over-counted readers (it counted _G.X, comments and mock field assignments) and its 'move to files[tests/]' remedy is wrong. libs/ and tests/_kit/ are excluded from lint, and spot checks agree with the reality lens: those names have no bare reader in linted files. Leaving them whitelisted hides real false negatives, such as the legacy UIDropDownMenu_AddButton. The fix is cheap, and it was already flagged once before (F-016).
findings.verdict_remediation: Remove the 44 read_globals with no bare reader in any linted file (the reality-lens list: _G, GetTime, GetTimePreciseSec, GameFontNormal, GameFontHighlight, GameFontDisable, STANDARD_TEXT_FONT, hooksecurefunc, securecallfunction, issecretvalue, C_Timer, C_Spell, C_SpecializationInfo, GetLocale, InCombatLockdown, PlaySound, UnitCastingInfo, UnitChannelInfo, UnitExists, UnitCanAttack, UnitGUID, UnitName, UnitIsDead, IsLoggedIn, UISpecialFrames, UIDropDownMenu_AddButton, CreateColorFromHexString, WrapTextInColorCode, CopyTable, wipe, tContains, tinsert, tremove, strsplit, strtrim, strjoin, date, time, BackdropTemplateMixin, CreateFromMixins, NORMAL_FONT_COLOR, HIGHLIGHT_FONT_COLOR, RED_FONT_COLOR, GREEN_FONT_COLOR). Keep the 24 bare-read names. Do not add a files["tests/"] read_globals stanza. Re-run luacheck and confirm 0/0; restore any name luacheck then flags.

findings.title: Module files reach into other modules' tables at file load; AnalyticsCharts extends NS.Analytics without idempotent publish
findings.category: architecture-§3 (MUST idempotent publish + SHOULD NOT file-load call)
findings.evidence: AnalyticsCharts.lua:2 binds local Analytics = NS.Analytics with no NS.Analytics = NS.Analytics or {} and writes Analytics._charts at :226. Escrow mutates Reconciler step lists at load; Timeline reads TM.TOTAL at load; Panel reads NS.Schema.MASTER_GROUP at load. Code cause of LH-78..81.
findings.remediation: Add NS.Analytics = NS.Analytics or {} in AnalyticsCharts; move Escrow step registration to an init/call-time read; read TM.TOTAL lazily; then mark the TOC lines conventional.
findings.cluster_title: LootHistory — ledger correctness, perf and architecture
findings.assessment: Verified: AnalyticsCharts.lua:2 is the only Analytics* file without `NS.Analytics = NS.Analytics or {}`. Escrow appends to R.SCAN_STEPS/R.PLAN_STEPS at load, Timeline reads TM.TOTAL at load and Panel reads MASTER_GROUP at load. These depend on TOC order, which is deterministic and correct. Only Escrow's mutation really fits the SHOULD NOT, and refactoring it into an init hook would put ledger step ordering at risk for no gain.
findings.verdict_remediation: Add `NS.Analytics = NS.Analytics or {}` at modules/AnalyticsCharts.lua:2. findings.title: One raising deferred secure write aborts the flush and orphans every later key for the session
findings.evidence: Flush calls each queued closure with no per-entry isolation; a raise stops the loop, later keys stay in pending but are gone from pendingOrder, and RunSecure never re-appends them, so in-combat writes for those keys are dropped until /reload; also skips NS.PublishVisibility(); diagnostics report pending=0. No known trigger today (candidates: SetPoint loop in Anchor.Apply, F-003).
findings.remediation: C-002: run each deferred write isolated (pcall), fully consume pending/pendingOrder regardless, log ungated to console and report via geterrorhandler(); add tests.
findings.cluster_title: PartyFrameEnhanced — secure-write queue robustness and profile rebuild
findings.assessment: Verified at :92-106. pendingOrder is swapped before the loop, but pending[key] is cleared only for the entries already reached. A raise therefore leaves the later keys stranded in pending, and RunSecure's `if not pending[key]` guard never re-appends them. Their in-combat writes are silently dropped until /reload, PublishVisibility is skipped, and PendingSecureCount reports 0. No trigger is known, so severity drops from medium to low. It is still worth fixing, because this queue carries every protected write the addon makes and the failure is silent for the whole session.
findings.verdict_remediation: In flushSecure, first snapshot and clear both pending and pendingOrder. Then run each closure through xpcall(fn, geterrorhandler()) so the error still reaches BugSack or the default handler, and continue with the remaining entries. OnLeaveCombat and StandUp must still reach PublishVisibility after the flush. Add a headless test in which a raising entry is followed by a normal one. It should assert that the second entry runs, the queue ends empty, and a later in-combat RunSecure on the raising key re-queues it.

findings.cluster_title: PartyFrameEnhanced — secure-write queue robustness and profile rebuild
findings.assessment: Confirmed at modules/SecureFollow.lua:194-201. The unwrap is pcall'ed but the restoring SecureHandlerWrapScript is not, which is inconsistent with Wrap's own guard at :173. A raise here is reachable only when another addon's OnAttributeChanged wrap is outermost on the same frame, and nothing in the collection does that. The PFE-R-02 fix removes the queue-orphaning consequence. What remains is a partial unwrap pass, which is minor.
findings.verdict_remediation: Fold this into the PFE-R-02 work item and do not give it its own item. If changed, wrap the re-wrap in xpcall(..., geterrorhandler()) so the unwrap loop continues and the failure stays visible. Do not pcall it and discard the error.
