findings.title: LootHistory's cached loot/currency patterns go stale whenever PrettyChat rewrites the chat globals mid-session
findings.evidence: LootHistory compiles patterns from LOOT_ITEM_SELF*, LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF*, LOOT_ITEM_REFUND*, CURRENCY_GAINED* on first parse and never invalidates. PrettyChat rewrites those globals on every settings write, profile change, /pc disable|enable, and every combat boundary under inCombat/outOfCombat visibility. Loot/currency records silently lost until /reload. PrettyChat docs call it handoff H-1, but LootHistory has no issue and its HEAD b9c1271 has no invalidation. Smoke OVR-9.
findings.remediation: Fix in LootHistory core/Util.lua (U-1): record source strings beside the compiled patterns, compare on parse and rebuild on difference (also RollWonPattern); add a LootHistory test swapping _G.LOOT_ITEM_SELF; open a LootHistory issue citing H-1. No PrettyChat code change (no bus message, per architecture-§4). Route: LootHistory (sibling addon, not an upstream).
findings.cluster_title: PrettyChat — cross-addon globals, settings validation, savedvars and comments
findings.assessment: Verified in LootHistory/core/Util.lua. Line 152 (lootPatterns or Build...) and line 215 (currencyPatterns) build their patterns once, and lines 170-179 cache rollWonPattern, including a cached false when the global is absent. PrettyChat rewrites those globals on settings writes, profile changes, enable and disable, and at combat boundaries, so self-loot and currency records are silently lost until /reload.
findings.verdict_remediation: In LootHistory core/Util.lua, store each global's source string beside its compiled pattern. On every parse, compare the stored string with the current _G value and rebuild when it differs. Apply this to loot, currency and RollWonPattern, and do not leave a cached false in place when the global changes. Add a LootHistory test that swaps _G.LOOT_ITEM_SELF in the middle of a session. Open a LootHistory issue that cites PrettyChat handoff H-1, and track the work under a LootHistory id. PrettyChat needs no code change. Only refresh the stale Util.lua line citations in PrettyChat docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:202.

findings.title: LineChart draws unclipped and ChartMath.Dashes is unbounded: one far off-plot point in a dashed range creates unbounded permanent Line regions
findings.locations: LibKa0s/WidgetsLineChart.lua:212 (dash loop), :236 (CreateLine), :362 (no clip), :369 (host yMin/yMax trusted); tests/test_widgets_linechart.lua:111
findings.evidence: Headless: Dashes(0,0,0,1e5) -> 14,286 dashes; Dashes(0,0,0,1e6) -> 142,858 dashes, 22 MB. In client each dash is a session-lifetime Line region (header :224). findings.remediation: C-01: clip every series segment and marker rule to the plot rectangle before drawing (bounds region count by geometry); CHART_MINOR 2->3; add out-of-domain cases. Rejected: clamping input, capping Dashes alone, documenting as host duty. Ships in v1.71.0.
findings.cluster_title: LibKa0s: Chart widget rendering and hover
findings.assessment: Confirmed in code: Math.Dashes (:205) is uncapped, and dashed() (:253) pools one session-lifetime Line per dash, with no clip to the plot rect. It cannot be reached today, because LootHistory, the only host, derives its x/y domain from its own series. So this is latent library-contract hardening, not a medium defect.
findings.verdict_remediation: Make the change only in the same chart-minor bump as LK-R-03. Clip each segment to the plot rectangle in one place, in the segment/dash emitter (Liang-Barsky), before dashing, so the dash count is bounded by plot geometry. findings.title: Chart hover does not resync on SetData/Render; every host must call ClearHover before repainting

findings.cluster_title: LibKa0s: Chart widget rendering and hover
findings.assessment: SetData/Render (:409-410) leave __hoverIndex and the crosshair alone, and HoverAtPixel (:430) re-fires only when the index changes. Pane resize runs TL:Layout -> chart:Render without ClearHover, so even the current host shows a stale crosshair pixel under a resting cursor. The defect is cosmetic, the fix is about two lines, and it removes a trap for every future host.
findings.verdict_remediation: In WidgetsLineChart.lua, have render() (reached from SetData/Render/OnSizeChanged) reset __hoverIndex to nil so the armed OnUpdate re-evaluates the hover against the new scale and data on the next frame. Ship it in the CHART_MINOR 3 bump with LK-R-01. Add a headless test: hover, Render at a new size, then assert the crosshair and onHover re-fire. LootHistory's explicit ClearHover can stay, since it is idempotent. Update the API doc's 'host must call ClearHover' note to say this is no longer required. The only change in addons is the re-vendor.

findings.title: Chart owns OnSizeChanged->Render, so a host rendering from its own layout pass may draw twice (unverified)

findings.remediation: Deferred by the review: measure first (headless count of Render calls per TL:Layout in LootHistory's suite, or in-client capture); change the seam (e.g. opts.manualRender) only if the number justifies it.
findings.cluster_title: LibKa0s: Chart widget rendering and hover
findings.assessment: This is not unverified. Pane OnSizeChanged runs TL:Layout, which calls chart:Render explicitly (Timeline.lua:332). The anchored chart's own OnSizeChanged (WidgetsLineChart.lua:463) also renders, so every pane resize renders twice. The cost is bounded: pooled regions, one extra LTTB pass and repaint, resize only. Nothing justifies a library seam such as opts.manualRender.
findings.verdict_remediation: Do not change LibKa0s. If addressed at all, do it host-side in LootHistory: in TL:Layout, skip the explicit chart:Render when the chart's size changed (its own OnSizeChanged already renders), or render explicitly only after SetData. Otherwise leave it until a headless Render-count measurement or a perf capture shows it matters.

findings.title: Autocomplete hooks installed once per box die silently on a later SetScript; re-calling lib.Autocomplete cannot reinstall them
findings.evidence: hooked[box] stays true after a host/skin SetScript replaces the script and its HookScript wrappers, so the documented recovery never re-hooks. OnTextChanged replaced -> list never opens; OnEditFocusLost/OnHide replaced -> list stays up. API doc does not state scripts must be set before the call; only LootHistory's BrowserFilterBar.lua:426 comment does. Both adopters (LootHistory, BankLedger) set scripts first, so not reached today. Mock may not model SetScript clearing hooks (unverified).
findings.remediation: C-03: re-install hooks on every lib.Autocomplete call behind a per-box generation so stale hooks go inert; document the set-scripts-first precondition in the API doc; fix testkit/mock_base.lua (+tests/_kit mirror, kit revision bump) only if the mock does not drop hooks on SetScript.
findings.cluster_title: LibKa0s — Autocomplete hooks, callbacks and options
findings.assessment: The mechanism is real. hookBox (WidgetsAutocomplete.lua:345-349) never re-hooks, so a later SetScript drops the hooks and they stay dropped. The API doc does not promise that re-calling recovers the box (docs:1216-1219 say 'hooked once per box'), but it also never states the set-scripts-first precondition. testkit/mock_base.lua:155 SetScript already overwrites HookScript wrappers, so the mock needs no change. Both adopters set their scripts first, so the severity is low.
findings.verdict_remediation: C-03: add to the 'Hooks, never scripts' bullet in docs/api/Widgets that the host must set the box's scripts before calling Autocomplete, because a later SetScript on a hooked script drops the hooks and re-calling does not reinstall them. Optional: re-hook on each call behind a per-box generation so that older wrappers do nothing, with tests that a re-call after SetScript works and that a re-call without SetScript does not double-dispatch. No mock or testkit change.

findings.title: Autocomplete calls host provider and onPick unprotected, unlike the library's other host callbacks

findings.cluster_title: LibKa0s — Autocomplete hooks, callbacks and options

Only tooltipPlace is pcall'd, because it has a defined fallback. A raising provider reaches geterrorhandler() with a stack trace that names the host's function, so wrapping it would only hide host bugs.

findings.title: ka0s-bounded timeout kills only the top process, then reports the run as stopped
findings.evidence: timeout --foreground signals only the direct child; forked children survive and keep the slot-pool lock fd (opened :78). Reproduced: KA0S_KIT_TIMEOUT_S=2 KA0S_KIT_CGROUP=off ka0s-bounded bash -c 'sleep 47; echo done' -> rc=124 'was stopped', pgrep still lists sleep 47; same with systemd scope (sleep 53 survivor). Softened in collection: LibKa0s kit gives each Lua process its own timeout. No timeout test case.

findings.title: ka0s-bounded computes the slot count once, before the wait loop
findings.evidence: slots=$(( avail_mb*6/10/slot_mb )) computed once; poll loop only probes slot.1..slot.$slots. A caller started under memory pressure with slots=1 waits for slot.1 even after memory frees; runs serialize more than needed in parallel sweeps.
findings.remediation: C-08: recompute slots (re-read MemAvailable) inside the wait loop; explicit KA0S_KIT_SLOTS still wins; print 'waiting' once.
findings.cluster_title: dev-copilot: ka0s-bounded runner and bounded-runs hook
findings.assessment: The slot count is computed once from a single MemAvailable read before the wait loop, so a caller that started under memory pressure stays serialized on slot.1. The only effect is slower parallel sweeps, never a wrong result.
findings.verdict_remediation: If done, recompute the slot count from MemAvailable inside the wait loop only when KA0S_KIT_SLOTS is unset, and print the 'waiting' message only once.

findings.cluster_title: dev-copilot — line-ending hook safety and tests
findings.assessment: The bug is real. perl -i at normalize-eol.sh:68/:76 replaces a symlink with a regular file and leaves the target unconverted, and the [[ -f ]] guard at :32 follows links. No Ka0s repo has a tracked symlink, so in the collection the bug is latent. The hook is global, though, and the fix is about three lines, so it should be done.
findings.verdict_remediation: In scripts/normalize-eol.sh, right after the empty and -f guards (:31-32) and before file_dir, repo_root, abs_file and rel_path are computed (:35-41), resolve the path with file_path="$(readlink -f -- "$file_path")" || exit 0. Then re-check [[ -f "$file_path" ]] || exit 0. With this order, the target's own repo and .gitattributes decide the ending, and perl rewrites the real file. A target outside any repo already exits at the repo_root guard. Land it after the red symlink case in DC-R-06.

findings.title: finalize's push-rejection recovery path (git pull --ff-only) can never succeed
findings.evidence: At 3e local default carries an unpushed --no-ff merge (or 3c commit); a rejection means origin moved, so histories diverge and --ff-only must fail. The 'fast-forwards' branch is unreachable; outcome is safe (stops) but the spec describes an impossible recovery and costs a doomed pull.
findings.remediation: C-10: on rejection stop that repo, report verbatim, leave the merge to the user; never --force, rebase or merge origin in.
findings.cluster_title: dev-copilot — command correctness (issues, cross-addon, new-addon, finalize)
findings.assessment: Verified at finalize.md:114. Whenever 3e has something new to push (the merge from 3d or the commit from 3c), a rejection means the histories have diverged, so --ff-only always fails. It succeeds only in the degenerate case where nothing local is unpushed, and then the push is moot. The current text is safe because it stops on failure, so fixing it only makes the spec accurate.
findings.verdict_remediation: On push rejection, stop that repo. Optionally git fetch to show how far origin moved, report the push output verbatim and leave the merge to the user. Never --force, rebase or merge origin in.
